name: Ajvar
intro: One jar. Red peppers, charred and cooked down, the way autumn has always kept them.
card_uses: Spoon it over a rice bowl.
Spread it on toast under an egg.
Put it next to anything roasted.
ingredients: 1 tbsp red wine vinegar or lemon juice
method: Char the peppers and the whole eggplant on a gas burner, grill, or under the broiler, turning until they're black all over and the eggplant collapses — the same dry-flame move from July and August. Put the peppers in a covered bowl for fifteen minutes, then peel and seed them. Split the eggplant and scoop out the flesh. Chop both finely by hand, or pulse a few times; it should stay rough, not smooth. Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-low, add everything else, and cook, stirring often, for 20 to 30 minutes, until the relish thickens, darkens, and the oil starts to separate at the edges. Taste: it should be sweet, smoky, and sharp. Spoon it into a jar and pour a thin layer of oil over the top. The idea underneath is the one worth keeping: char, peel, then cook it down slowly until the water is gone and the flavor is concentrated. That's how a vegetable becomes something that keeps.

storage.note: Keeps two weeks in the refrigerator under a thin layer of olive oil. Use a clean spoon, and top up the oil when you take some out.

uses.label: Rice bowl
uses.context: It's a sauce and a vegetable at once. Roasted squash and arugula finish the bowl.
